293131.title: Chuncheon Ani-Toy Festival
293131.overview: A three-day subculture fair at the Animation Museum in Chuncheon, gathering animation, characters, art toys, figures, goods, and creator content in one place. Brand and artist booths, industry experience programs, and sales floors run side by side, bringing companies, creators, fans, and collectors together — with plenty for families in between the collector stalls. Free, 11:00–17:00 over the early-October holiday weekend.

3011445.title: Creative X Seongsu
3011445.overview: A culture-and-creative-industry festival spread across Seongsu-dong — Seoul's converted-factory district often compared to Brooklyn. Anchored at the S-Factory, the program mixes themed exhibitions by culture-tech companies, conferences and pitches, 'Play Seongsu' turning the whole district into a game theme park, gallery exhibitions, a craft flea market, an outdoor fashion show, and an urban music festival. Fees and hours vary by program — check before you go, then let the neighborhood's cafes fill the gaps.

2990881.title: Gwangju Busking World Cup
2990881.overview: An international street-music competition staged across downtown Gwangju, centered on the May 18 Democracy Plaza. Buskers from Korea and abroad — vocalists, bands, acoustic acts, performers — battle through preliminaries and finals judged by a professional panel, turning the city's streets into open stages for days. Free, 13:00–22:00; the finals nights draw the biggest crowds.

232325.title: Hoengseong Hanwoo Beef Festival
232325.overview: Hoengseong hanwoo is arguably Korea's most famous beef brand, and this five-day riverside festival is its showcase — the 22nd edition, themed 'delicious, stay, shine'. The grill zone is the main event: buy fresh hanwoo at festival prices and cook it on the spot. Around it run 14 programs across food, culture, and hands-on themes, with day (10:00–18:00) and night (18:00–21:00) programming designed to keep visitors on site. Free entry; the beef is what you pay for — happily.

3009344.title: Naju Yeongsangang River Festival
3009344.overview: Naju's five-day autumn festival in the Yeongsangang Garden, where the wide river meets landscaped grounds. Days bring garden strolls, family programs, and Naju food (the city is famous for its beef-broth gukbap and pears); nights turn to illuminated riverscapes and headline performances. A stay-all-day festival that doubles as an introduction to one of Jeolla's oldest river towns. Free, 11:00–21:00.

563458.title: Hamyang Wild Ginseng Festival
563458.overview: Hamyang's mountain-grown ginseng — raised above 500m in germanium-rich soil, dense-fleshed and high in saponin — is billed as Korea's premium sansam, backed by the country's first wild-ginseng traceability system. The festival unfolds in Sangnim Park, a 1,100-year-old planted forest and Natural Monument, with programs reviving the culture of the simmani (wild-ginseng hunters), local-produce markets, and forest-and-culture events. Free, 10:00–21:00; the ancient forest alone justifies the visit.

1105347.title: Jeongeup Gujeolcho Flower Festival
1105347.overview: Every October, 150,000 square meters of white gujeolcho (Korean chrysanthemum) bloom beneath a pine forest along a clear mountain stream in Jeongeup — the largest such garden in the East, and one of Korea's most beloved photography spots, whether in dawn mist or afternoon light. Walking paths thread the pine-scented flower hills, joined by local-heritage experience programs and farm-produce markets. Ticketed entry, 08:30–17:30.

1365782.title: Jeungpyeong Insamgol Festival
1365782.overview: Jeungpyeong grows about two-thirds of Chungbuk's ginseng, and its harvest festival has grown into a full-spectrum event: the 'In-Maek Party' pairing ginseng with beer and EDM, an international youth festival, a national song contest, a national busking festival, and nightly fireworks. Family and health experience zones, on-site produce auctions, and traditional ssireum wrestling round it out. Free, 10:00–20:00 along the Bogangcheon sports park.

141236.title: Saenggeo Jincheon Culture Festival
141236.overview: Jincheon's folk festival, running since 1979 on the Baekgokcheon riverside — the county's biggest annual event, drawing tens of thousands. The name comes from the old saying 'saenggeo Jincheon': the best place to live. Folk-arts competitions, a local-food cook-off, ssireum wrestling, performances, exhibitions, hands-on programs, and a food market fill the grounds, with the county's famously abundant farm produce on sale throughout. Free, 09:00–22:00 (varies by day).

1718137.title: Silla Culture Festival
1718137.overview: Gyeongju's flagship festival since 1962, now in its 53rd edition, staged among the city's actual Silla monuments. The Hwabaek ceremony reenacts royal history against Woljeonggyo Bridge; a street-arts festival and Silk Road Festa fill the historic quarter; and the Hwarang Hip-hop Festa puts Korea's top hip-hop acts on stage in front of ancient burial mounds — a collision of eras you will only see here. The Moonlight Market adds local food into the night. Free, 15:00–24:00.

2622679.title: 8th Yecheon International Smartphone Film Festival
2622679.overview: A film festival for movies shot entirely on smartphones — the device 'everyone' carries — running in Yecheon since 2019 and now Korea's flagship smartphone-film event. Entries from an open international call are judged and screened, with the awards ceremony and a community film-festival day on October 9. Free, 11:00–20:20, in a green county better known for archery and old pavilions.

3113001.title: Daejeon Donggu-dongnak Festival
3113001.overview: A festival behind Daejeon Station, spreading through the east plaza and along the Daedongcheon stream — the gateway to Soje-dong's retro cafe alley and the old railway officials' village. World-food theme booths, all-ages game zones, a streamside 'booknic' of books and rest, a bakery competition (this is the city of bakeries), and chef cooking shows give it an urban, food-forward flavor distinct from Korea's rural festivals. Free, 11:00–22:00.
3113001.place: Soje-dong east plaza and Daedongcheon stream

2408959.title: Incheon Open Port Heritage Night Tour
2408959.overview: The 11th night festival in Incheon's open-port quarter — the district of 1880s customs houses, banks, and warehouses where modern Korea first met the world. The classic '8 nights' program (night views, night roads, night history, night food, night market and more) threads performances, exhibitions, and food through three evenings of specially opened heritage buildings, with lodging promotions for those who stay. Free, 18:00–22:00; Chinatown and Songwol-dong's fairytale village are next door.

2828336.title: Siheung Wolgot Port Festival
2828336.overview: A harbor festival at Wolgot, the fishing port folded into the city on Gyeonggi's west coast. The draws are hands-on: fishing-boat rides, bare-hand fish catching, and king-prawn catching, plus surprise seafood auctions, a dried-seafood wholesale market, and salted-shrimp making. Evenings bring the Moonlight Concert and opening and closing fireworks over the water. Free, 10:00–22:00 — Seoul's nearest taste of working-port festival culture.

2877244.title: Welcome to Singwan-dong
2877244.overview: A youth street festival on the university strip of Singwan-dong in Gongju, run since 2022 as part of the city's culture-city initiative. Busking competitions, street performances, a beer festa, flea markets, and hands-on programs line the college road, with students, residents, and merchants co-running the show. Timed alongside the Baekje Culture Festival, so you can pair ancient-kingdom pageantry with a student-quarter night out. Free, 14:00–21:00.
2877244.sponsor: Gongju City · Gongju Culture & Tourism Foundation

3370635.title: Hwasun Jeokbyeok Culture Festival
3370635.overview: Hwasun Jeokbyeok — the 'Red Cliffs' rising over a reservoir in a restricted watershed — is one of Jeolla's most striking and least-accessible landscapes, and this festival is the easiest way in. Programs include guided cliff walks, the GEO environmental concert, wellness sessions under the cliffs, local-produce markets, and community programs, with free shuttle buses running to the site. Free (some programs paid), 10:00–17:00.
3370635.place: Iseo Community Center and Hwasun Jeokbyeok cliffs

3011280.title: Seoul Design Week 2026
3011280.overview: Seoul's design festival, in its 13th year, runs 12 days under the theme 'The Design Recipe'. The DDP Design Fair stages a 'market of tastes' where visitors assemble Seoul-found brands around their own preferences, while exhibitions span DDP, Seongsu, and Hongdae: works by 100 working Seoul designers, international studio process shows, and goods pop-ups full of 'next Seoul'. Early bird 9,000 won, regular 15,000 won; 10:00–20:00.
3011280.place: Dongdaemun Design Plaza and venues in Seongsu and Hongdae

604454.title: Gochang Moyang Fortress Festival
604454.overview: Gochang Eupseong (Moyang Fortress) is Korea's best-preserved town wall, and its festival is built on a charming legend: circle the wall once to cure leg ailments, twice for long life, three times for paradise. The signature dapseong wall-walk becomes a nighttime moonlight round combined with the ganggangsullae circle dance, joined by a 1,000-resident street parade, the 'Returns 1453' time-travel program inside the fortress, and markets of Gochang specialties. Free, 10:00–22:00.

3522254.title: Chungbuk Garden Expo in Yeongdong
3522254.overview: The second Chungcheongbuk-do garden expo lands in Yeongdong — the county of gugak (traditional music) and fruit — for four days at Yongdu Park. Garden-industry exhibitions, experience and flea-market zones, and garden-culture performances share the grounds with citizen-made gardens selected by open call, all threaded with live gugak. It deliberately overlaps the Nangye Gugak Festival, so traditional music carries across both events. Free, 09:00–18:00.

553263.title: 30th Ulsan Whale Festival
553263.overview: Jangsaengpo was once Korea's whaling capital; today its Whale Culture Special Zone celebrates coexistence instead, and the festival turns 30 with the theme 'The whale's invitation — a 30th birthday party!'. Four days bring a whale parade, themed performances, a 300-citizen chorus, special fireworks, kids' festa, AR and AI whale experiences, an anniversary archive exhibition, and food zones — plus year-round attractions like the whale-watching cruise and ecology hall. Free, 10:00–21:00.

1844150.title: Chilgok Nakdonggang Peace Festival
1844150.overview: Chilgok was the last line of defense in the 1950 Battle of the Nakdong River, and this festival — the 13th — honors that history under the slogan 'a boy becomes a boy soldier', spotlighting the young student-soldiers often left out of the heroic narrative. Peace-themed performances, participatory programs, and food zones fill the Chilgokbo eco-park, co-organized with the Second Operations Command. Free (some programs paid), 10:00–22:00.
1844150.sponsor: Chilgok Culture & Tourism Foundation · ROK Second Operations Command

2551117.title: Gimhae Heritage Night Tour
2551117.overview: A night festival among the monuments of Gaya — the ancient kingdom whose royal tomb of King Suro, Daeseong-dong tumuli, and Sureungwon garden anchor central Gimhae. The '8 nights' program lights the heritage quarter with night views, story walks, performances, exhibitions, food, and markets, letting visitors meet Korea's 'fourth kingdom' — the one that never made the standard Three Kingdoms narrative — on atmospheric terms. Free, 16:00–23:00.
2551117.place: King Suro's Tomb and Sureungwon area
2551117.sponsor: Korea Heritage Service · Gyeongsangnam-do · Gimhae City

1275743.title: Geumjeongsanseong Fortress Festival
1275743.overview: Geumjeongsanseong is Korea's largest mountain fortress, ringing the peaks above Busan — and with Geumjeongsan newly designated a national park in 2026, this year's festival celebrates both. Three days of history, culture, and arts programs at the fortress plaza commemorate the wall's construction, blending the mountain's ecology with its military heritage. Running since 1996. Free (some programs paid), 10:00–19:00; combine with the fortress-village makgeolli, a Busan institution.

900168.title: Boeun Jujube Festival
900168.overview: Boeun's jujubes were once royal tribute goods, and its 20th-anniversary festival is one of Korea's top farm-produce events — a three-time provincial best-festival winner. The riverside park at the foot of Songnisan National Park fills with jujube and produce markets (plus an online store and fresh-jujube call center for nationwide delivery), performances, and family programs. Free, 10:00–20:00. Pair it with Beopjusa Temple and Songnisan's autumn leaves for a full day.

1344850.title: King Sejong & Chojeong Mineral Water Festival
1344850.overview: In 1444, King Sejong — creator of the Korean alphabet — spent 120 days at the Chojeong springs treating his ailments while continuing affairs of state. The festival celebrates that history at the restored Chojeong Haenggung (temporary palace), on the site of one of the world's three most famous naturally carbonated springs. Court reenactments, wellness programs, and hands-on booths fill the culture park. Free entry (some experiences paid), 10:00–21:00.
1344850.place: Chojeong Culture Park and Chojeong Haenggung

3007256.title: Jeonggwan Eco-Stream Culture Festival
3007256.overview: A three-day community festival along the Jwagwangcheon — the garden stream running through Busan's Jeonggwan new town. Eco-stream experience programs put visitors in direct contact with the waterway's plants and wildlife, alongside sketching and writing contests, a parade, a family walking event, and performances and exhibitions that turn residents' daily riverside into a festival stage. Free, 10:00–20:00.

3331805.title: NS Food Festa
3331805.overview: A food-culture festival at Harim's First Kitchen campus in Iksan, co-hosted by NS Home Shopping. Korea's largest amateur cooking competition anchors the program, joined by chef cooking shows, regional-produce tastings and sales, family performances — and the 'gourmet tour', a live look inside one of Korea's most advanced food-production facilities. Free, 10:00–17:00. A distinctly industrial-modern take on the Korean food festival.

2667707.title: 14th Gyeonggi Garden Culture Expo
2667707.overview: A garden expo at Dumulmeori — the celebrated confluence where the North and South Han Rivers meet — and Semiwon, the province's first designated local garden, famous for its lotus ponds. The 2026 theme, 'Dumulmeori: four colors of thought', uses the palette of the seasons to frame both nature's cycle and quiet self-reflection along the paths linking the two sites. Free, 10:30–17:00. One of the most scenic day trips on the Seoul commuter rail line.

3020205.title: Ho-Camp Returns
3020205.overview: A family camping festival in its ninth year, organized by the camping YouTube channels Ho-Camp, GogoTwoMing, and Hong-Camp at the Neowaduri farm campground in Okcheon. The weekend runs a welcome party, singing contest, laser-tag survival games, a second-hand camping-gear auction, a kids' cinema, party night, and prize giveaways. Participation is per family (from 180,000 won for two adults and two children) — book ahead; it is a committed camping crowd.
3020205.fee: From 180,000 won per family (2 adults + 2 children)

2933008.title: Buan Red Sunset Festival
2933008.overview: The west coast at Byeonsan Beach turns crimson at dusk, and this three-day festival is built around that view: a red-wine festa and jazz festival against the sunset, a children's song contest, and a kite carnival of giant kites over the autumn sky. Sea breeze, music, wine, and the reddening horizon — aimed equally at families and couples. Free, 10:00–21:00, on the Byeonsan Peninsula's most famous beach.

3017799.title: Gumi Food Festival
3017799.overview: Started in 2022 to lift spirits and small businesses after the pandemic, Gumi's food festival packs the Songjeong food street with some 200 menu items — one of the largest spreads on the Korean festival circuit — plus performances and children's content across all age groups. Free entry (some zones paid), 12:00–20:00 in the city center.

2833186.title: Siheung International Youth Festival (SIYF)
2833186.overview: Korea's largest youth-club festival: some 584 clubs and 7,800 teenagers from Siheung's youth-club support program plan and run the entire event themselves — performances, experiences, exhibitions, and exchange programs spanning volunteering, academics, sports, dance, bands, and the arts. International youth groups join through exchange partnerships, giving it a growing global dimension. Free, 13:00–21:00 at Siheung City Hall.

2756476.title: Royal Tombs of Joseon World Heritage Festival
2756476.overview: The UNESCO-listed royal tombs of the Joseon dynasty — 12 tomb clusters around Seoul and Gyeonggi, from Donggureung to Yeongwol's Jangneung — open up for ten days of tours, performances, exhibitions, and experience programs, each built on the particular story of its tomb. Now in its 7th year, the festival is the rare chance to see these serene, forested royal grounds animated after hours. Entry and program fees vary by site.
2756476.place: 12 Joseon royal tomb sites (Donggureung, Seooreung, Yungneung·Geolleung and others)
2756476.sponsor: Royal Palaces and Tombs Center, Korea Heritage Service

3530139.title: 2026 Chungnam Drone Festa
3530139.overview: A drone omnibus on the provincial-office plaza in Hongseong: a national drone competition of precision-piloting and search missions open to all comers, an industry conference, exhibition and piloting-experience zones — and the headliner, a light show of more than 1,200 drones animating the province's vision across the night sky. Free, 10:00–21:00.

234232.title: Sacheon Air Show
234232.overview: The largest air show in southern Korea, held at Sacheon Airfield in the city that hosts Korea's aerospace agency and KAI, the national aircraft maker. Four days of flight demonstrations (including the Black Eagles aerobatic team in past editions), an aerospace-and-defense industry exhibition, aircraft and military-equipment displays, experience flights, academic sessions, and competitions spanning public, business, and government audiences. Free, 09:00–17:00.
234232.sponsor: ROK Air Force · Gyeongsangnam-do · Sacheon City · KAI

1075049.title: 17th Art Gwangju International Art Fair
1075049.overview: The Honam region's largest international art fair, filling the Kimdaejung Convention Center with around 110 galleries from 12 countries across painting, sculpture, and media art. Special exhibitions — a masterpiece show, collector 'propose' show, and rising-star showcase — broaden it beyond a sales floor, connecting Gwangju's contemporary-art scene (home of Asia's leading biennale) with international galleries and collectors. On-site tickets from 15,000 won (online cheaper).
1075049.fee: Adults 15,000 won on site (10,000 online) · VIP and youth rates available

4046174.title: Chiaksan Hanwoo Beef Festival
4046174.overview: Wonju's beef festival, run by the local livestock cooperative around the premium Chiaksan hanwoo brand raised in the clean air below Chiaksan National Park. Tastings and discounted sales are the core draw, joined by regional-produce markets, family programs, and local performance stages. Free entry (beef paid), 11:00–21:00 — the 12th edition of a reliably delicious regional fixture.

2591661.title: Yeoncheon Job's Tears Festival
2591661.overview: Yeoncheon is Korea's home of yulmu (Job's tears), the nutty grain brewed into one of the country's favorite warm drinks, and its festival sells the harvest at the source — set, remarkably, on the Jeongok-ri Prehistoric Site where Acheulean hand-axes rewrote Asian archaeology. Farm sales, agricultural-culture experiences, exhibitions, performances, and country-market food give it an old-school rural fair feel. Free, 10:00–17:00.

2828537.title: Tteokbokki Festival
2828537.overview: Korea's flagship festival for its favorite street food, hosted by Daegu's Buk-gu at the iM Bank Park stadium grounds — three days, tens of thousands of visitors, and tteokbokki from famous vendors nationwide. Beyond the food zone: main-stage concerts, the 'Tteok-Fe Night', spicy-red lucky draws, a finish-your-tteokbokki challenge, and even a dedicated inbound tour program for Taiwanese visitors. Free entry, 11:00–21:30. Come hungry, leave red-lipped.

506616.title: Seogwipo Chilsimni Festival
506616.overview: Seogwipo's signature citizens' festival, filling the old downtown and the Cheonjiyeon Waterfall area with a street parade — the centerpiece, joined by residents and community groups — plus multi-genre performances, busking, local-artist stages, food, and flea markets. 'Chilsimni' (seventy ri) is the poetic old measure of the town's reach, and the festival works as a walking tour of Seogwipo's harborfront identity. Free, 10:00–22:00.
506616.place: Cheonjiyeon parking area and old downtown

2872078.title: Incheon Film Week 2026
2872078.overview: A film festival reviving Incheon's identity as a cradle of early Korean cinema, under the theme 'we are each other's future'. Three days at CGV Incheon Yeonsu pair a curated slate of films about people running toward their futures with family-friendly side programs. Free; the detailed schedule posts on the festival website ahead of opening.

3521741.title: Seoul BBQ Festival
3521741.overview: K-BBQ gets its own urban festival at Nanji Campground on the Han River. The self-BBQ zone hands you ingredients and grills with no gear required; 'BBQ Masters' brings star chefs to the fire; and BBQ Village gathers famous restaurants worth queueing for — all run 'campnic' style, camping-meets-picnic. Regional produce, desserts, performances, and experience programs fill the rest of the grounds. Ticketed; 12:00–21:00.

4106717.title: 13th 21st Century Human Values Forum
4106717.overview: A humanities forum in Andong — Korea's Confucian heartland — themed 'a shaken world, the things that do not change'. Three days of keynote lectures, scholar and citizen sessions, exhibitions, tours, and networking take on war and peace, memory and record, AI and technology, closing with the proclamation of the Andong Declaration. Around 5,000 participants join on site and online. Free, 10:00–20:00 (times vary by day).
4106717.sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism · Gyeongsangbuk-do · Andong City

3501104.title: Seongnam-dong Coffee Festival
3501104.overview: Ulsan's old downtown of Seongnam-dong — where mid-century tearooms once nurtured the industrial city's literary scene — hosts a citizen coffee festival run by the district's cafe owners and baristas. Hand-drip demonstrations, latte-art experiences, brewing contests, brand tastings, a national barista performance competition, live music, and food markets fill the culture street. Free, 10:00–20:00.

639648.title: Yesan Apple Festival
639648.overview: The 23rd Yesan apple festival moves to Yedang Lake, home of Korea's longest pedestrian suspension bridge, pairing the region's famous apples with its biggest landmark under the theme 'a sweet day at Yedangho'. Apple wine and desserts meet jazz, gugak, and classical crossover stages, while the two-day 'Apple Sale Festa' — run by the growers' cooperative — sells premium fruit at farm prices. Free, 10:00–20:00.

3383613.title: Goyang Haengju Hanwoo BBQ Festival
3383613.overview: Goyang's livestock cooperative throws a one-day charcoal-grill festival for Haengju hanwoo, the city's premium beef brand. Free tastings of charcoal-grilled beef anchor the event, with quality-controlled cuts sold direct from farms and family entertainment alongside — a compact, appetite-driven local festival rather than a sprawling production. Free, 10:00–17:00.
3383613.place: By Goyang Fire Station (Jugyo public lot)

3400809.title: Fisherman's Market X Port Village Tongyeong
3400809.overview: Tongyeong — Korea's seafood capital on the southern coast — pairs its fisherman's market with the Port Village food-festival brand for three days on the triathlon plaza. Booths build menus around the port's signature catch: oysters, eel, sea squirt, red seabream; performance booths cook live in front of you; and chef-consulting booths develop new dishes with name chefs. Free entry, 10:00–21:00, with the city's famous harbor food alleys minutes away.

3492576.title: Busan Illustration Fair V.7
3492576.overview: The southern edition of Korea's leading illustration fair, run by the organizers of the Seoul Illustration Fair at BEXCO. Around 600 booths span illustration, painting, picture books, independent publishing, character design, graphics, games, animation, webtoons, and calligraphy, with popular Korean and international creators selling originals and goods directly. Adults 11,000 won (early bird 6,000); children free.
3492576.fee: Adults/teens 11,000 won · Early bird 6,000 won · Children free

1087020.title: Brotherly Love Festival
1087020.overview: Yesan's Daeheung township is home to the beloved Korean folktale of two brothers who secretly carried rice sheaves to each other's fields by night — and this family festival retells it through storytelling programs, traditional games, family events, performances, and a local-food market at the Brotherly Love Park. The Yedang Lake suspension bridge and monorail are nearby for a full county day out. Free, 10:00–20:00.

1391363.title: Hwasun Unjusa Culture Festival
1391363.overview: Unjusa is one of Korea's most enigmatic temples — the 'valley of a thousand Buddhas and a thousand pagodas', where carved stone figures and towers dot the hillsides and a giant reclining Buddha lies unfinished per its legend. The autumn festival fills the tranquil grounds with bell-ringing, pungmul percussion, multi-genre concerts, temple-wide mission games, and traditional culture programs. Free, 10:00–17:00 — worth the trip for the temple alone.

4101384.title: 20th Century Photography Masters: Light, Stopping Time
4101384.overview: Eighty original physical prints by 17 masters who built modern photography — Henri Cartier-Bresson, Tina Modotti, William Klein among them — drawn from the Gallery Lumiere collection. In an age of disposable digital images, the show insists on the weight of the analog print: silver-salt and platinum textures carrying the air and temperature of the moment the shutter fell. A meditative counterpoint to the scrolling feed, at Art Chosun Space near City Hall. Adults 12,000 won; 50% off on Culture Day.
4101384.fee: Adults 12,000 won · Youth/seniors 9,000 won · Infants free

3368470.title: Gyeonggi Rice Dessert Festa
3368470.overview: A dessert expo championing Gyeonggi rice as a baking ingredient: rice bakeries and rice-tteokbokki makers gather at Suwon Messe with sales zones, competitions, and hands-on programs promoting a healthier rice-based dessert culture. Free, 11:00–17:00 — a niche but tasty window into Korea's rice-flour baking boom.

4095478.title: Busan Bridge Marathon
4095478.overview: A winter road race through the marine city, gathering at BEXCO with two distances: a full marathon (entry requires a verified sub-4:30 finish from another race) and a 10km open to anyone 18 or older. The course shows off Busan's bridges and waterfront in the crisp December air. Full course 80,000 won, 10km 60,000 won; start 07:30.
4095478.sponsor: Busan Metropolitan City · Korea Athletics Federation · KNN
